critical_code_review_comments: DUPLICATE data-testid: DifferentiationSection renders BOTH desktop (lg:grid) and mobile (stacked) layouts in the DOM and each layout uses the same data-testid='diff-step-0..3'. Tests saw dup_count=2 for every step. Only one layout is visible per viewport (Tailwind hides the other), so end-users are unaffected, but automation must use .first and regression scripts can be fragile. Recommend suffixing (e.g. diff-step-0-desktop / diff-step-0-mobile) or rendering only one tree per breakpoint.

ValueStackSection: the fade-in Savings card animation has transition delay=2.2s — it's above-the-fold fine, but the 2.2s delay means users scrolling fast see the card appear late. Consider reducing the delay or anchoring animation to in-view rather than mount time.

chat.py admin_chat_insights: MongoDB $trim only strips from the ENDS of the normalized string — punctuation in the middle (e.g. 'hola, qué es quantro') is preserved, so two slightly-different phrasings will still not fold together. Grouping works for the sample spec because leading '¿' and trailing '?' are the only non-alphanumerics. If you want deeper grouping, either pre-normalize at write time or use $regexReplace in the pipeline.

chat.py: created_at is stored as ISO string. The range query for the insights window works only because the ISO format is lexicographically sortable in UTC zulu form. Prefer BSON datetime + an index on created_at for scale.

ValueStackSection SavingsCard uses useInViewTween but the hook is NOT gated by inView — the tween starts on mount, not when the card scrolls into view. The visual delay=2.2s masks this, but the counter animation can finish before the user ever sees it. Gate with an IntersectionObserver or useInView.
seed_data_creation: Module-scoped pytest fixture inserted 2 chat_messages with session_id prefix 'TEST_sess_*' and contents '¿Qué es Quantro?' and '¿qué es quantro'. Fixture teardown deletes both by _id — no residual test data.

rca of the issue: No product bugs found. One test-logic gotcha was resolved: MongoDB $trim only strips chars from string ends (like Python str.strip), so placing a unique marker suffix containing '?' inside the seeded content broke grouping — fixed by using spec-exact samples and identifying by session_id + normalized equality.
